name: Pier and warehouses
blurb: A planned harbor target at a port town.
history:
A pier is a raised structure, usually on piles or pillars, that juts out from the shore over the water, giving boats a place to dock and passengers and cargo a way on and off. Its open structure lets tides and currents flow through, unlike the solid foundation of a quay.

In North America and Australia, where many ports were long built on the multiple-pier model, the word usually implies a cargo-handling facility.
